quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane you choose.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you check for vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What do larger vehicles have compared to smaller vehicles?

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Cut across traffic quickly to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely, then reverse to return to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. Go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and wait until the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and continue with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed carefully. You do not have to stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road ahead curves back and forth. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: Is it true that you should be careful passing large vehicles and avoid staying beside them for long periods?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay next to a large vehicle for long. Either move ahead or fall back for safety.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look for traffic, then go if clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and continue carefully.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: A term for blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with restrictions on car stereos.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A term for blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, back, and front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait for the light to change.
Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may go in the direction the green arrow points if you are in the correct lane. Before you turn, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and both sides constantly.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and both sides constantly.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on spotting problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if there is an oncoming car, if a hill or curve blocks your view, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no-pass zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both hazards at once.

questions.question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you safely pass a bicyclist?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space.
Keep driving. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of bikes. Do not pass too fast or close. Honking may startle riders and cause a crash.

questions.question: You may use your horn when you:

options.text: Need to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Lose control of your car.
Are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound the horn to alert other drivers.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chance of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for vehicles with disability plates, disabled veteran plates, or disability placards.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or switch drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or switch drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or switch drivers if you feel tired. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They are gone if you have side mirrors on both sides.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: What do orange background signs mean?

options.text: General warning signs.
Construction and maintenance warning signs.
Regulatory signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: What colors are highway exit distance signs?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Destination signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Drive to the right edge and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: When driving in fog, should you use low beam headlights?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crash risks?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks because you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The only safe choice is to decide before drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions once you have started drinking.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
They brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. Following too closely puts both your life and the motorcyclist's life at risk. You need enough distance to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist has to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you move left or right. Use your signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign prohibiting it.

questions.question: Is it good to turn your head and check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: No, it is a bad driving habit.
Yes, it is a good driving habit.
No, it is unnecessary.
No, not if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road ahead?

options.text: Keep your speed to drive through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles to prevent skidding. A dry, solid surface is always the safest for driving.
